properties.name: A release that has gone out and records shipping nothing is reported
properties.statement:
A Release that is pinned to an epoch and deployed, and carries no INCLUDES edge, shall be reported as a gap — a release record claiming to have shipped nothing.

THE SCHEMA HAS ALWAYS SAID THIS AND NOTHING ENFORCED IT. The INCLUDES extraction hint ends: "The as-released view is read off these edges; a Release with none is a version number, not a manifest." That sentence described a state the design could not detect.

MEASURED, AND THE COST WAS A PUBLISHED RELEASE. On 2026-08-21 v0.38.0 was tagged, built, published and asset-verified with 0 INCLUDES against v0.37.0's 275. `release_includes_all` defaults to a dry run — correctly, so a cut can read what it is about to package — and its reply carries "applied": false beside "added": 304. The 304 is a forecast. It was read as an accomplishment twice, and every check that ran passed over the empty manifest: isError false both times, reflow2_check green, release_report never called.

THE DEFECT IS THAT A DRY RUN AND A WRITE ARE INDISTINGUISHABLE TO EVERY CHECK THAT RAN. This is `rule:success-is-read-from-the-authoritative-object` failing on a third surface after `gh pr merge`. The detector is that reading, performed by something that cannot forget to perform it.

THE RULE MUST NOT CONSULT `status`, and that is the load-bearing clause. Its sibling `release_without_epoch` exempts a `planned` release because an epoch is minted at the cut. Carrying that exemption here would have exempted the one real instance: rel:v0380 was published and deployed while its status still read `planned`, because nothing makes anyone move it. A status property records what somebody remembered to write down; a DEPLOYED_TO edge records that the thing went out.

ASKED, NEVER REPAIRED. What a release shipped is a judgement, and a genuinely contentless release — a re-tag, a docs-only republish — is a real state to accept. apply_heal must not invent a manifest (`cap:no-fabricated-repair`).

DISTINCT FROM the TemporalFact recording the v0.38.0 incident: that says what happened once, on a dated occasion, to one release; this says what the design shall detect from now on, for every release. DISTINCT FROM the capability that delivers it: that describes the mechanism built, its severity and its guards, and could be replaced by a different mechanism without this obligation changing.
